facts.fact: 笑话长期靠口耳相传，在酒馆与篝火边被反复讲述，并不总被认为值得写下来
facts.anchor: Historically, jokes have been passed around orally, told and retold in taverns and around campfires, and not always seen as worth preserving in written form.

facts.fact: 已知最古老的笑话距今仅四千年
facts.anchor: the oldest that historians are aware of dates back a mere 4,000 years

facts.fact: 公元前 1900 年苏美尔的“最古老笑话”：一个年轻女子没在丈夫腿上放屁，作者承认它性别歧视且并不好笑
facts.anchor: ‘Something which has never occurred since time immemorial; a young woman did not fart in her husband’s lap.’

facts.fact: 作者对古埃及那条（公元前 1600 年，法老、渔网、尼罗河）的评价同样是“很烂”
公元前 1200 年苏美尔有一条包袱失传的笑话，译者成了真正的笑柄
facts.anchor: There’s the text of a joke surviving from that era that has the punchline missing

facts.fact: 马其顿的腓力二世曾让人把雅典一个俱乐部的笑话全部记下，但同样失传
facts.anchor: Philip II of Macedon (in modern-day Greece) arranged for a members’ club in Athens to write down all their jokes for him

facts.fact: 现存最早的笑话集 Philogelos（“爱笑”）编于公元 250–400 年，收 264 条编号笑话
facts.anchor: The earliest surviving joke book, Philogelos (which translates from Greek as ‘Love of Laughter’) was compiled sometime between 250 and 400 CE.

facts.fact: 古书里生菜笑话特别多，因为古人相信生菜是春药
facts.anchor: due to the ancient belief that it was an aphrodisiac

facts.fact: 印刷术发明后出现真正出版的笑话书，Poggio Bracciolini 1470 年代的 Facetiae 被认为是最早一本
facts.anchor: with 1470s Facetiae by Poggio Bracciolini thought to be the first
